newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesman seeks no new claims against former chief.
newsitem.headline: Mannesman seeks no new claims against former chief.

text.p: German industrial concern Mannesmann AG said on Wednesday its supervisory board has decided to drop any further damage claims against former chief executive Werner Dieter.
Dieter resigned in 1994 after he was suspected of fraud. In September he agreed to pay one million marks ($668,000) to settle the case, but admitted no guilt.
He was suspected of channelling lucrative orders from Mannessmann's hydraulic equipment subsidiary, Rexroth GmbH, to Hydrac GmbH, a components maker owned by Dieter's family.

Mannesmann also said Wolfgang Peter, the management board member responsible for its automobile products, will oversee technology as well. Peter replaces Klaus Czeguhn, who resigned for personal reasons, Mannesmann said. ($ = 1.496 German Marks)
